keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «자율 주행차에는 신뢰라는 큰 과제가 있다(문제)» 와 «자율 주행차는 기술이 안전하다고 증명되고 사람들이 그것을 믿게 될 때에만 성공한다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (there is a big challenge: trust) and the conclusion (self-driving cars will only succeed if the technology proves safe and people come to trust it). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Self-driving cars and whether people can trust them
Fewer crashes from human error, and more freedom for elderly and disabled people
Unusual situations, unclear responsibility, and hackers make trust difficult

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

sum.pre: Self-driving cars use cameras, radar, and other
to understand the road. Supporters say they could save lives, because human
plays a role in most crashes. However, a big challenge is
: the cars can be confused by unusual situations, and it is unclear who is
when an accident happens. Most countries are introducing the technology step by step, with strict
. These cars will succeed only if they prove safe and people trust them.

devices that notice light, sound, movement, or heat
human error, such as distraction or tiredness
something that takes your attention away

qs.q: Why might a computer drive more safely than a tired person?
qs.qko: 컴퓨터가 지친 사람보다 왜 더 안전하게 운전할 수 있나요?
opts: Because a computer never gets sleepy, angry, or distracted
Because a computer always drives faster
Because a computer can never be confused
evs: Computer programs then decide when to speed up, slow down, or turn.
A computer never gets sleepy, angry, or distracted by a phone.
Self-driving systems can still be confused by unusual situations, such as heavy snow, road construction, or a person behaving unexpectedly.
Not a single car finished, and the best one traveled only about 12 kilometers.
why: 컴퓨터는 졸리거나 화가 나거나 휴대폰 때문에 한눈을 팔지 않아요. 그래서 지친 사람보다 더 안전하게 운전할 수 있다고 봐요.
A computer never gets sleepy, angry, or distracted by a phone, so it may drive more safely.

qs.q: In the text, what do 'levels of automation' describe?
qs.qko: 글에서 'levels of automation(자동화 단계)' 는 무엇을 나타내나요?
opts: How fast a car can drive on the highway
How much of the driving a car can do by itself
How many sensors a car carries
evs: These cars use cameras, radar, and other sensors to understand the road around them.
Engineers often describe levels of automation from zero, meaning no automation, to five, meaning the car can drive itself everywhere.
Just one year later, five cars completed the course.
When an accident does happen, it is also unclear who should be responsible: the passenger, the car company, or the software designer.
why: 엔지니어들은 자동화 단계를 «0(자동화 없음)» 부터 «5(어디서나 스스로 운전)» 까지로 설명해요. 차가 운전을 얼마나 스스로 하는지를 나타내요.
Engineers describe levels from zero (no automation) to five (the car drives itself everywhere). They show how much the car drives by itself.

qs.q: Why is it hard for people to trust self-driving cars?
qs.qko: 사람들이 자율 주행차를 믿기 어려운 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: They are too slow and cannot turn corners
They can be confused in unusual situations, and it is unclear who is responsible after an accident
evs: Self-driving systems can still be confused by unusual situations, such as heavy snow, road construction, or a person behaving unexpectedly.
Supporters argue that self-driving cars could save many lives.
When an accident does happen, it is also unclear who should be responsible: the passenger, the car company, or the software designer.
Imagine getting into a car, telling it where to go, and reading a book while it drives you there.
why: 자율 주행 시스템은 폭설이나 도로 공사 같은 낯선 상황에서 헷갈릴 수 있고, 사고가 나면 누가 책임져야 하는지도 분명하지 않아요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
The systems can be confused by unusual situations, and it is unclear who is responsible after an accident. You need both sentences.

ends: Who should be responsible when a self-driving car crashes?
자율 주행차가 사고를 내면 누가 책임져야 할까?
How do self-driving cars see the road in snow or rain?
자율 주행차는 눈이나 비 속에서 어떻게 도로를 볼까?

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «해야 할 일 + 그 목적» 으로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what we should do and the result you want in English.
write.src: “We should <u>test self-driving cars carefully</u> so that <u>people can trust them on the road</u>.”

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «so that» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을 할 수 있게» 를 넣어 목적을 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: so that older people can travel safely)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «so that», write who + what they can do to make the purpose clear. (e.g. so that older people can travel safely)
